hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A peak at index j requires nums[j - 1] < nums[j] > nums[j + 1].

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Record the indices of all peak positions in the array.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: For each peak p[k], a valid range must include p[k] but exclude adjacent peaks p[k - 1] and p[k + 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def countSinglePeakSubarrays(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    peaks = []
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if nums[i - 1] < nums[i] > nums[i + 1]:
            peaks.append(i)
    if not peaks:
        return 0
    ans = 0
    m = len(peaks)
    for k in range(m):
        cur = peaks[k]
        left_bound = (peaks[k - 1] + 1) if k > 0 else 0
        right_bound = (peaks[k + 1] - 1) if k < m - 1 else n - 1
        left_choices = cur - left_bound + 1
        right_choices = right_bound - cur + 1
        ans += left_choices * right_choices
    return ans
```

complexity.notes: Finds peaks in linear time and calculates valid endpoint combinations for each peak in O(1).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating O(n^2) subarrays with peak count checks takes quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores peak indices of size at most n.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Calculates Cartesian product of valid left and right bounds per peak.
